title: Open projection/base-change square on the finite and completed domains
statement:
Fix $k=\overline{\mathbf F}_q$, a prime $\ell\ne\operatorname{char}k$, a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$, its valuation ring $R=\mathcal O_E$, a uniformizer $t$, and $A_n=R/t^n$, $n\ge1$, with the operation datum of [def-sf-datum]. Let $X,\overline X,Y,Y'$ be finite-type $k$-schemes, let $j:X\hookrightarrow\overline X$ be open, $p:\overline X\to Y$ proper, and $g:Y'\to Y$ a $k$-morphism. Put $\overline X'=\overline X\times_Y Y'$, $X'=X\times_Y Y'$, and write $p':\overline X'\to Y'$, $h:\overline X'\to\overline X$, $j':X'\hookrightarrow\overline X'$ and $a:X'\to X$ for the projections and induced open immersion. Use either $\Lambda=A_n$ in the ordinary small pro-etale module derived categories, or $\Lambda=R$ in the derived-complete constructible categories, with completed pullback and tensor [def-weil-derived-pullback-tensor-hom, def-weil-derived-complete-integral-detailed]. Let $K\in D^b_c(X,\Lambda)$ and $L\in D^b_{ctf}(Y,\Lambda)$; no finite-Tor hypothesis is imposed on $K$. Set
$$F=Lp^*,\quad F'=Lp'^*,\quad G=Lg^*,\quad H=Lh^*,\quad A=La^*,\quad J=Lj^*,\quad J'=Lj'^*,\quad S=Rp_*,\quad S'=Rp'_*,$$
$$M=j_!K,\qquad P=FL,\qquad Q=M\otimes P.$$
Use the canonical tensor comparisons $\mu_u$ and pullback-composition comparisons of [lem-pur-derived-pullback-tensor-iso], with $\theta:F'G\cong HF$ and $\sigma:AJ\cong J'H$. Use precisely the open maps $\beta_N:Hj_!N\cong j'_!AN$ and $\gamma_{j;N,T}:j_!N\otimes T\cong j_!(N\otimes JT)$ of [def-exchange-projection]; their completed interpretation retains the strict quotient transitions. Composition below is right to left.

At $\Lambda=R$, all objects appearing in the following equations, and the objects $SM,SQ,S'HM,S'HQ$, are bounded constructible derived-complete objects. In particular $j_!K$ and $j'_!AK$ are bounded constructible, and the ordinary adjunctions and canonical tensor comparisons on those domains are defined. At finite coefficients the equations are in the ambient derived categories; the displayed tensors involving $L$ lie on the bounded constructible domains.

For $B,C\in D^b_c(Y,R)$, or arbitrary $B,C\in D(Y_{\mathrm{proet}},A_n)$ at finite level, the specified square comparison obeys
$$\mu_{H;FB,FC}\,H(\mu_{F;B,C})\,\theta_{B\otimes C}=(\theta_B\otimes\theta_C)\,\mu_{F';GB,GC}\,F'(\mu_{G;B,C}).$$
Put
$$z_{K,P}=j'_!\bigl((1\otimes\sigma_P)\mu_{A;K,JP}\bigr)\beta_{K\otimes JP}.$$
Then the actual open maps satisfy, naturally in $K,L$,
$$z_{K,P}\,H(\gamma_{j;K,P})=\gamma_{j';AK,HP}(\beta_K\otimes1)\mu_{H;M,P}.$$
Both sides are morphisms $H(j_!K\otimes P)\to j'_!(AK\otimes J'HP)$. This is an equality of completed morphisms at $R$, before rationalization or finite evaluation.

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-Q26-319016ab9 (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: I read the whole delivery. It has no new nodes, the item statement is byte-identical to its base (an unsplit Q119 node with no proof), and no repair note exists. stmt_deps adds def-weil-derived-direct-image, which is right because the statement uses Rp_*. The proof follows the base-change paragraph of main-20261015 prop-sf-pf-coherence.proof.md: on the j_! factor, both composites lie in the essential image of j'_! and restrict to the identity. Step by step: (1) finite pullbacks along A and H preserve D^b_c with no separatedness assumption on g, using exactness, the pulled-back stratification and local constancy of the pullback; j_! preserves D^b_c with its interval. (2) Finite Tor is used only for L along p and j, both separated (j is quasi-compact because the scheme is Noetherian); lem-sf-tensor-ctf(i) needs only one ctf factor, so K may have infinite Tor amplitude. (3) The integral domains come from integral-operations-preserve-constructible, clause (2) of open-factor-coherence, and integral-direct-image-constructible for p and p'; the pushforward and monoidal-adjunction comparisons say what the step takes from them. (4) θ-monoidality: I recomputed μ_HF·θ=(θ⊗θ)·μ_F'G from the composition clause, so the elementary flag is fine. (5) Detection by J' through full faithfulness of j'_! holds at A_n (open-tensor-normalization) and at R (open-factor clauses 1 and 3). (6) I recomputed both restricted routes; each equals d=(1⊗σ_P)μ_A in the given coordinates. Every arrow type-checks. Edge cases checked: X empty, j=id, g=id, K=0 or L=0, n=1, and K of infinite Tor amplitude. Advisory nit: step 1 does not say that X→Y is finite type (p is proper, and j is quasi-compact on a Noetherian scheme). Accepted tool_uses: the 11 generic domain, closure and normalization lemmas listed in review.md; the two pur comparison nodes are on the route through sk-lem-sf-mate and sk-prop-sf-pf-reduction. Batch-5: I walked the closure from both targets without expanding the item, the nt-assume leaves, the trf/pod chapters or sk-thm-trace-transport. All three flagged citations are already in that closure (monoidal-adjunction-transport via lem-fix-compactification-completed-realization; pushforward-comparison via lem-sf-integral-direct-image-constructible; open-factor-coherence via the a1/zl chain), and the item adds 0 nodes. The named forbidden nodes (pod derived exact-square pasting, completed scalar regularity, trf functorial flat resolution) are generic infrastructure, not steps of the trace formula or Poincaré duality. No SGA, no cycle, no new nodes, so no duplicates.
